title: Order Details with Customer and Product Names
description:
Join orders, customers, and products tables to produce a full order report showing customer name, product name, category, and order amount.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`

**Table: products** — `id`, `name`, `category`

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `product_id`, `amount`

Output columns: `order_id`, `customer_name`, `product_name`, `category`, `amount`. Order by `order_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice'),(2,'Bob'),(3,'Carol'),(4,'Dave'); CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Widget A','Electronics'),(2,'Shirt X','Clothing'),(3,'Book 1','Books'),(4,'Gadget Y','Electronics'); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, product_id INT, amount DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,1,49.99),(2,1,3,14.99),(3,2,2,29.99),(4,2,4,79.99),(5,3,1,49.99),(6,3,2,29.99),(7,4,3,14.99),(8,4,4,79.99);
solution_sql: SELECT o.id AS order_id, c.name AS customer_name, p.name AS product_name, p.category, o.amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id ORDER BY o.id

test_cases.description: 8 orders joining 4 customers and 4 products — 8 rows with full details

hints: Chain two JOIN clauses: first join orders to customers, then join the result to products.
Use table aliases (o, c, p) to keep the query readable and avoid column name ambiguity.
explanation: The first JOIN connects orders to customers via customer_id. The second JOIN connects to products via product_id. Order 1: Alice bought Widget A (Electronics) for 49.99. Order 4: Bob bought Gadget Y (Electronics) for 79.99. All 8 orders have valid customer and product references so all 8 rows are returned by INNER JOIN.
